描述_EN: by the second half of the 16th century, the portuguese had succeeded in acquiring a trading base at macau (off canton) from the chinese government, where trade from china and japan passed through. it is supposed that the woven pattern here may have been made by japanese or chinese sojourners in macau, according to patterns given to them to follow. however, the floral scrolls patterns bear stronger resemblance to east asian floral scrolls, suggesting that this may have been woven by chinese (or even japanese) weavers for an export market. the colour scheme adopted in this woven pattern is also similar to that found on some portuguese handwoven silk. this piece of silk fragment, woven in three colours in the width (red, blue and yellow, now faded), has european features, such as the double-headed bird that occurs frequently in portuguese textile designs.
描述_ZN: 到16世纪下半叶，葡萄牙人已经成功地从中国政府那里获得了一个位于澳门（广州附近）的贸易基地，来自中国和日本的贸易在这里通过。 据推测，这里的编织图案可能是由日本或中国在澳门的旅居者根据给他们的图案制作的。 然而，花卉卷轴图案与东亚花卉卷轴更为相似，这表明这可能是由中国（甚至日本）织工为出口市场编织的。 这个编织图案所采用的颜色方案也类似于一些葡萄牙手织丝绸上的颜色。 这块丝绸碎片在宽度上用三种颜色（红、蓝、黄，现已褪色）织成，具有欧洲特色，如葡萄牙纺织品设计中经常出现的双头鸟。
